doc.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Why jazz history is important
summary: Gitler says the music and its musicians matter and that jazz, born as Afro-American expression, opened people's minds to others' humanity.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I want to open with a question and ask you why is jazz history important?

Well it’s important because the music is important so we should keep track of what happened and, you know, the lives of the musicians and the breadth of the music over the years. But also because of the way it ties in with our culture. It’s so part of our culture, and it’s been such a great — not just an entertainment and an artistic enjoyment, but it’s been a way of bringing people together and enlightening people about people. Because let’s face it, jazz began as an Afro-American expression, and because of what the great musicians of that tradition put down in the twenties and the thirties and even before, it opened the eyes and minds as well as the ears to people of other persuasions and it showed something of the humanity and the intellect of these people, where ordinarily some other people might not have made this connection.
